A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In a Dutch national study, 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once stereotactic radiotherapy was fully available. That is about the effect our model assumes, but the change in the share of all patients is our own calculation.
supported_en: Annals of Oncology (2012, Netherlands Cancer Registry): 7% fewer elderly stage I patients untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show the 0.8-point gain across all lung cancer patients, or any figure for Finland or Kainuu.
in_use_quote: Paikallisessa tai paikallisesti edenneessä taudissa, jos leikkaushoito ei ole mahdollista, voidaan antaa täsmäsädehoitoa tai yhtä aikaa säde- ja solunsalpaajahoitoa eli kemosädehoitoa.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every frail stage I patient is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says the university hospital runs the lung cancer team meetings and gives the surgery and radiotherapy. When surgery is not possible, precision radiotherapy (täsmäsädehoito, the Finnish term for stereotactic radiotherapy) can be given. Kainuu's own pages say its patients get radiotherapy at OYS, and some get it in Kuopio. A Dutch national registry study (Annals of Oncology, 2012) found 7% fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated once this treatment was fully available.
unanswered_en: I found no written rule, at OYS or in Kainuu, that every stage I patient too frail for surgery must be referred for stereotactic radiotherapy, and no figure for how many such patients go untreated.

verdict_en: Partly in place in the OYS university hospital area, which treats Kainuu's patients. Supported: Annals of Oncology (2012, Netherlands Cancer Registry): 7% fewer elderly stage I patients untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available. Not supported: The pages do not show the 0.8-point gain across all lung cancer patients, or any figure for Finland or Kainuu.
